newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ANGELS SIGN GARRET ANDERSON TO THREE-YEAR DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ANGELS SIGN GARRET ANDERSON TO THREE-YEAR DEAL.

text.p: The Anaheim Angels and left fielder Garret Anderson have agreed on a three-year contract with a club option for the 2000 season, the team announced Friday. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The 24-year-old Anderson hit .285 with 33 doubles, two triples, 12 homers and 72 RBI in 150 games for the Angels last season. He became the first Angel to have a six-hit game on September 27, at Texas.

A lifetime .300 hitter, Anderson has 28 homers and 142 RBI in 261 games. In 1995, Anderson finished second to Minnesota's Marty Cordova for American League Rookie of the Year by batting .321 with 10 homers and 69 RBI in 106 games.
It appeared that his job in left field might be in jeopardy last season when California brought up the number one overall pick in the 1995 draft, Darin Erstad.
But Anaheim decided to move Erstad to first base this season and leave Anderson with centre fielder Jim Edmonds and right fielder Tim Salmon, who together form one of the league's best outfields.
